trust_decision.summary: The buffer's capacity check decides whether the space reserved for a write is really free. In IO mode, after the 512-byte stack buffer is grown to FBUFFER_IO_BUFFER_SIZE, the early return compares `requested < capa` but ignores the bytes already held (fb->len), so the caller writes past the heap allocation. The check is in fbuffer_do_inc_capa.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'generator heap buffer overflow when streaming to an IO'. Searching for fb->io leads straight to the IO branch of fbuffer_do_inc_capa.

fix_sites.entry_point: every generator call (fbuffer_stack_init, renamed fbuffer_init, now skips the stack buffer when an IO is given)
every buffer write in IO mode (fbuffer_do_inc_capa, reached through fbuffer_inc_capa)
JSON::State#generate(obj, io) and #_generate_no_fallback; also JSON::Coder#dump(obj, io) via lib/json/common.rb:1080
JSON::State.generate(obj, opts, io); also JSON.dump(obj, io) via lib/json/common.rb:958

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix sites are one header plus the two init call sites in generator.c, all in the same extension. java/src/json/ext/Generator.java:98-100 is a JVM implementation (BufferedOutputStream, bounds-checked) and is not affected; lib/json/truffle_ruby/generator.rb:347 is pure Ruby.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is nothing plausible to dismiss: every write goes through the single fbuffer_inc_capa/fbuffer_do_inc_capa check, so fixing that check covers all entry points at once.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: IO streaming must keep flushing in FBUFFER_IO_BUFFER_SIZE chunks (rb_io_write), not grow one unbounded buffer. Non-IO generation must keep the 512-byte stack fast path and honour buffer_initial_length. An over-broad fix (always heap-allocate, or never flush) still passes correctness tests; only the coupling of the stack path with flushing is subtle.

O6_input_shapes: IO target with a first large write after earlier small output (len > 0 while the stack buffer is grown to the IO size)
a single write larger than FBUFFER_IO_BUFFER_SIZE (falls through to the doubling loop)
the class-method path (State.generate / JSON.dump) and the instance path (State#generate / Coder#dump)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A direct-pointer write in the SIMD string-escape fast path that reserves with its own size arithmetic and skips fbuffer_inc_capa.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code already writes through buf->ptr + buf->len after a manual reserve, so a maintainer chasing performance could plausibly drop or mis-size the reserve.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Float formatting writes into buffer->ptr + buffer->len after reserving a fixed 32 bytes; a variant could reserve less than the formatter emits in IO mode.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A fixed-size reserve sitting before a formatter is a common pattern and is easy to get wrong when the output format changes.

O9_family: memory-safety: heap buffer overflow from a wrong capacity calculation (CWE-131/787)

O10_build.toolchain: MRI Ruby with headers, rake-compiler (rake compile), C compiler
O10_build.project_tests: test/json/json_generator_test.rb (generator and buffer_initial_length tests; the fix diff adds no tests)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change the early return to `requested < fb->capa - fb->len`, or always heap-allocate in IO mode. Either fixes the single real sink, so the tempting fix is also a correct one.
